source_read: Publisher HTML full text (IEEE Access, open access), read 2026-11-24
hardware: Local machine: Intel Core i7-9850H CPU, 4 GB GPU, 32 GB RAM. No wearable or edge device
input_window: 90 frames with 10-frame overlap at 100 Hz; 3-axis acceleration from one lower-back IMU (KFall)
latency: about 20 ms per inference, all three phases (Kiran et al. 52 ms as cited)
latency_boundary: Model inference on the training workstation; the paper does not say whether the CPU or the GPU ran it or whether segmentation is included
energy_boundary: none: no energy or power figure is given
memory_size: not reported (a reduced LSTM variant is said to be about 72% smaller at about 3 points lower accuracy)
split: ?: five-fold cross-validation over windows; the unit of the split is not stated (32 subjects)
comparator_as_printed: Accuracy 97.0%, 36 classes, pre-impact only (Kiran et al. [20], Table 2); the running text of Section II-C gives 98% for the same work; literature value. Proposed: accuracy 98.0%
resource_basis: measured (named workstation; not the implied device)
notes: F1 98.02 / 98.19 / 98.61% for pre-impact, post-impact and transition. Simulated falls by young adults. On-device deployment is listed as future work.

hardware: Server: NVIDIA RTX 4090. Edge: Raspberry Pi 4, quad-core Cortex-A72, up to 4 GB RAM
runtime_precision: TensorFlow Serving (SavedModel) and TFLite; FP32, FP16, INT8
input_window: 30 s segments, 5 s stride, 256 Hz, 2 of 23 EEG channels (CHB-MIT)
latency: Student 66.83 ms (GPU), 153.165 ms (CPU), 83.839 ms (TFLite FP16), 52.710 ms (TFLite INT8); teacher 90.3 / 252.751 / 190.786 / 171.594 ms
latency_boundary: Stated as end-to-end inference, average ms per sample. Table V does not name the device per row; Section III-F assigns the GPU row to the RTX 4090 and the CPU and TFLite rows to the Raspberry Pi 4
energy_boundary: none: energy efficiency is asserted without a figure
memory_size: Teacher 16.7 MB, 2,181,410 parameters; student 0.17 MB, 21,000 parameters; TFLite 0.08 MB
networking: REST API to a remote dashboard on the server path; local alarm on the Raspberry Pi
split: R (adjudicated; second reader). Author reading: W for the headline (mostly patient-specific rows, overlapping 30 s windows at 5 s stride); S for the patient-independent row
comparator_as_printed: Accuracy 97.1% (pruned CNN, patient-independent, LightSeizureNet [24]); literature value
notes: The abstract's 97% is the student's validation average (0.970); held-out test average 0.958; patient-independent student test accuracy 0.922. INT8 lowers student accuracy to 85%.

hardware: Single NVIDIA H100 GPU (named for training under identical conditions). No edge device
latency: 260 ms per sample against 281 ms for BIOT, on TUEV
latency_boundary: Per-sample inference of the model; the inference device is not named separately from the training GPU
memory_size: parameter count shown only as bubble size in Fig. 1
split: S: official TUEV and TUSZ corpus splits; CHB-MIT reported subject-dependent and subject-independent
resource_basis: measured (datacenter GPU; not an edge result)
notes: Subject-independent CHB-MIT balanced accuracy 0.5747 against 0.5741 for BIOT, which the authors call comparable.

hardware: None physical: behaviour-level Simulink (level-crossing ADC) and ModelSim (spiking processor, Verilog) co-simulation
input_window: Per beat, 79 sampling points on average; 2-lead MIT-BIH, 360 Hz, converted to 4 spike channels
energy: not reported (relative claims only: 55.9x less data, 42.4x fewer FLOPs)
memory_size: 24.6 kFLOPs per inference (23,192 ADD + 1,430 MUL), 303 neurons; weight memory 60 kB against 513 kB flat
comparator_as_printed: ACC 95.5% (RSNN+SVM [7]), the strongest in Table I and above the proposed 95.34%; also Residual CNN [2] 93.4%, SCNN [3] 91%, MLP(LC) [5] 85.21%; literature values
resource_basis: estimated (adjudicated; second reader): analytic operation counts; the co-simulation gives no power or latency figure. Author reading: simulated
notes: Two leads, not a single ECG stream. Proposed accuracy 95.34%.

hardware: Training on two NVIDIA T4 GPUs (Kaggle). Latency on a single-thread CPU that is not named. No edge device
runtime_precision: FP32 and INT8 sizes given; no INT8 accuracy
input_window: 3000 samples = 10 s at 300 Hz, single lead (CinC 2017)
latency_boundary: Model inference on an unnamed single-thread CPU
memory_size: about 184,000 parameters; 38.94 MFLOPs; 19.47 MMACs; 780.81 kB FP32; 286.34 kB INT8
split: S as claimed (strictly at the patient level); the dataset has no public patient identifiers, so only record-level separation is supported, and Section II-A and Section III-A describe different splits
resource_basis: measured (adjudicated; second reader): latency timed on a single-thread CPU the paper does not name; FLOP and MAC counts are analytic. Author reading: estimated
notes: Single lead: spatio-temporal in the title refers to CNN features. FPGA and ASIC implementation is listed as future work.

hardware: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Developer Kit, 8 GB. Training on an RTX 4090
input_window: Stack of 10 frames, 640 x 640, one frame per 160 s over 24 min
latency: 87.06 ms inference; 113.47 ms end to end per stack
latency_boundary: Both boundaries are stated: model inference, and end to end per stack on the Jetson
energy: 11.05 W average system power; no energy figure in the main text
energy_boundary: System power on the Jetson during inference; energy per stack is not printed (about 1.25 J by multiplication)
memory_size: 2.62 M parameters; TensorRT engine 8.12 MB; peak GPU memory 5608 MB
networking: none; images come from a Raspberry Pi HQ Camera in the instrument
split: R (adjudicated; second reader). Author reading: ?: 355 stacks split 213/71/71; the split unit (chip or reaction zone) is not stated and patches overlap by 30 pixels
calibration: none (Fig. 3b is an assay concentration curve, not a probability calibration)
external_validation: none (agreement with a commercial dPCR system on the same instrument and lab)
notes: In-vitro nucleic acid quantification on a point-of-care instrument; no patient data.

hardware: 40 nm, 25 mW RRAM compute-in-memory SoC with Cortex-M3, taken from prior work (Chang et al., ISSCC 2022). Also an RTX 4050 laptop (80 W) and a Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB (5 W)
runtime_precision: 8-bit weights, binarized activations, step function in place of ReLU on the chip
input_window: 361 samples per beat, 4 x 361 spike image; 2-lead MIT-BIH, 360 Hz
latency: 5 us compute-in-memory inference; 0.81 ms preprocessing on an unnamed CPU
latency_boundary: The 5 us covers the compute-in-memory stage only; Section IV-C adds 0.81 ms preprocessing, so the abstract's end-to-end inference within 5 us is not end to end
energy: 100-150 uJ at 25 mW full power mode
energy_boundary: No measurement boundary or method is described. 25 mW x 5 us = 0.125 uJ, 800 to 1,200 times below the printed value; the GPU row is nameplate power times latency (80 W x 40 us = 3.2 mJ exactly)
memory_size: about 857 kFLOPs per inference; preprocessing about 3.5 kFLOPs
split: R (adjudicated; second reader). Author reading: W: 5-fold stratified cross-validation with intra-patient beat shuffling
resource_basis: estimated (mapped to a published chip; no measurement shown)
notes: The 98.61% accuracy is a PyTorch result; no accuracy is reported for the chip-deployed variant. Table II heads a column of watts Operating Voltage. The text cites Chu et al. as 95.34% and Table I prints 97.8% for the same reference.
